knowledge:
- key_parameters:
  - which=guidance ;; In withinLaneNormalization and betweenLaneNormalization, specifies the normalization method (e.g., "full" for full-quantile, "loess" for robust local regression, "median", or "upper" for upper-quartile scaling).
  - offset=guidance ;; In normalization functions, if set to TRUE, calculates and stores a normalization offset matrix instead of (or in addition to) modifying the counts directly.
  - round=guidance ;; In normalization functions, if TRUE (default), rounds normalized values to the nearest integer to produce "pseudo-counts". Set to FALSE to preserve exact decimal values and avoid rounding approximations.
  - org=guidance ;; In getGeneLengthAndGCContent, specifies the organism identifier (e.g., "hsa" for Homo sapiens, "sacCer3" for Saccharomyces cerevisiae) to retrieve gene metadata.
  - mode=guidance ;; In getGeneLengthAndGCContent, specifies the retrieval database/method (e.g., "biomart" or "org.db").
- alternatives:
  - ShortRead (FastqFileList)=guidance ;; Used for managing and reading raw unaligned FASTQ files.
  - Rsamtools (BamFileList)=guidance ;; Used for managing and reading aligned BAM files.
  - IRanges / Genominator / Rsubread=guidance ;; Mentioned as alternative packages for aggregating raw reads over genomic features to produce gene-level counts before using EDASeq.
  - edgeR / DESeq2=guidance ;; Preferred for downstream statistical modeling and differential expression analysis using EDASeq-normalized counts or offsets.
- when_to_use:
  - Use read-level EDA when you need to perform initial quality control on raw sequencing reads (FASTQ) or alignments (BAM) to identify low-quality lanes, sequencing depth issues, or nucleotide composition biases.
  - Use gene-level EDA and normalization when you have gene-level count data and need to diagnose and correct systematic biases (such as GC-content, gene length, and sequencing depth differences) before conducting differential expression analysis.
- pitfalls:
  - edgeR offset sign convention ;; edgeR expects the offset argument to be the log-ratio of raw to normalized counts, which is the negative of the offset calculated by EDASeq. You must pass `-offst(dataOffset)` to edgeR.
  - Over-dispersion diagnostics ;; The mean-variance relationship (via meanVarPlot) must be examined within replicate lanes only (conditional on experimental groups). Plotting across different biological conditions will artificially inflate dispersion due to true biological differences.
  - Row and column name alignment ;; When constructing a SeqExpressionSet, the row names of counts and featureData must be identical, and the row names of phenoData must match the column names of counts.
  - Zero counts in log-fold-change ;; To avoid log(0) errors, a small constant of 0.1 is added to counts during log-fold-change and offset calculations.

workflows.name: read_level_qc
workflows.intent: Perform quality control and exploratory data analysis on raw unaligned reads (FASTQ) and aligned reads (BAM).
workflows.stages:
1. Identify and list raw FASTQ or aligned BAM files.
2. Construct FastqFileList or BamFileList objects and attach sample metadata.
3. Generate barplots of total or mapped read counts per lane.
4. Plot mean per-base quality scores across sequencing cycles.
5. Plot per-base nucleotide frequencies to check for sequence composition bias.
workflows.code:
files <- list.files(file.path(system.file(package = "yeastRNASeq"), "reads"), pattern = "fastq", full.names = TRUE)
names(files) <- gsub("\\.fastq.*", "", basename(files))
met <- DataFrame(conditions=c(rep("mut",2), rep("wt",2)), row.names=names(files))
fastq <- FastqFileList(files)
elementMetadata(fastq) <- met
fastq

files <- list.files(file.path(system.file(package = "leeBamViews"), "bam"), pattern = "bam$", full.names = TRUE)
names(files) <- gsub("\\.bam", "", basename(files))
gt <- gsub(".*/", "", files)
gt <- gsub("_.*", "", gt)
lane <- gsub(".*(.)$", "\\1", gt)
geno <- gsub(".$", "", gt)
pd <- DataFrame(geno=geno, lane=lane, row.names=paste(geno,lane,sep="."))
bfs <- BamFileList(files)
elementMetadata(bfs) <- pd
bfs

colors <- c(rep(rgb(1,0,0,alpha=0.7),2), rep(rgb(0,0,1,alpha=0.7),2), rep(rgb(0,1,0,alpha=0.7),2), rep(rgb(0,1,1,alpha=0.7),2))
barplot(bfs,las=2,col=colors)

plotQuality(bfs,col=colors,lty=1)
legend("topright",unique(elementMetadata(bfs)[,1]), fill=unique(colors))

plotQuality(bfs[[1]],cex.axis=.8)
barplot(bfs[[1]],las=2)

plotNtFrequency(bfs[[1]])

workflows.name: gene_level_eda_and_normalization
workflows.intent: Diagnose gene-level biases (GC-content, length, over-dispersion) and perform within-lane and between-lane normalization on count data.
input: gene_metadata.tsv (GC-content and length for each gene)
workflows.stages:
1. Filter out non-expressed or low-count genes.
2. Construct a SeqExpressionSet object containing counts, feature metadata (GC-content, length), and sample phenoData.
3. Visualize count distributions using boxplots and mean-difference (MD) plots.
4. Check for over-dispersion using mean-variance plots.
5. Diagnose GC-content or length biases using bias plots and stratified boxplots.
6. Perform within-lane normalization (e.g., to correct GC-content bias) followed by between-lane normalization (e.g., to correct sequencing depth).
7. Alternatively, calculate and export normalization offsets for downstream differential expression analysis in edgeR or DESeq2.
workflows.code:
data(geneLevelData)
data(yeastGC)
data(yeastLength)

filter <- apply(geneLevelData,1,function(x) mean(x)>10)
common <- intersect(names(yeastGC), rownames(geneLevelData[filter,]))

feature <- data.frame(gc=yeastGC,length=yeastLength)
data <- newSeqExpressionSet(counts=as.matrix(geneLevelData[common,]),
                            featureData=feature[common,],
                            phenoData=data.frame(
                              conditions=factor(c(rep("mut",2),rep("wt",2))),
                              row.names=colnames(geneLevelData)))

head(counts(data))
pData(data)
head(fData(data))
head(offst(data))

boxplot(data,col=colors[1:4])
MDPlot(data,c(1,3))

meanVarPlot(data[,1:2], log=TRUE, ylim=c(0,16))
meanVarPlot(data, log=TRUE, ylim=c(0,16))

biasPlot(data, "gc", log=TRUE, ylim=c(1,5))

lfc <- log(counts(data)[,3]+0.1) - log(counts(data)[,1]+0.1)
biasBoxplot(lfc, fData(data)$gc)

dataWithin <- withinLaneNormalization(data,"gc", which="full")
dataNorm <- betweenLaneNormalization(dataWithin, which="full")

biasPlot(dataNorm, "gc", log=TRUE, ylim=c(1,5))
boxplot(dataNorm, col=colors)

dataOffset <- withinLaneNormalization(data,"gc", which="full",offset=TRUE)
dataOffset <- betweenLaneNormalization(dataOffset, which="full",offset=TRUE)

library(edgeR)
design <- model.matrix(~conditions, data=pData(dataOffset))
y <- DGEList(counts=counts(dataOffset), group=pData(dataOffset)$conditions)
y$offset <- -offst(dataOffset)
y <- estimateDisp(y, design)
fit <- glmFit(y, design)
lrt <- glmLRT(fit, coef=2)
topTags(lrt)

library(DESeq2)
dds <- DESeqDataSetFromMatrix(countData = counts(dataOffset), colData = pData(dataOffset), design = ~ conditions)
normFactors <- exp(-1 * offst(dataOffset))
normFactors <- normFactors / exp(rowMeans(log(normFactors)))
normalizationFactors(dds) <- normFactors
dds <- DESeq(dds)
res <- results(dds)
res

dataNorm <- betweenLaneNormalization(data, round=FALSE, offset=TRUE)
norm1 <- normCounts(dataNorm)
norm2 <- exp(log(counts(dataNorm) + 0.1 ) + offst(dataNorm)) - 0.1

getGeneLengthAndGCContent(id=c("ENSG00000012048", "ENSG00000139618"), org="hsa")
fData(data) <- getGeneLengthAndGCContent(featureNames(data), org="sacCer3", mode="org.db")
